subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the term 'mixed media' mean in art and design?
options: Using only one drawing material such as graphite
Combining two or more different materials or techniques in one piece
Copying an artwork exactly using tracing
questions.explain: Mixed media work combines two or more materials or techniques within a single artwork.

questions.q: Which of these is a collage technique that combines media?
options: Layering torn paper, fabric and paint onto a surface
questions.explain: Collage builds an image by layering and sticking varied materials such as paper, fabric and paint onto a support.

questions.q: Why might an artist add ink over a watercolour wash rather than using watercolour alone?
options: To make the paper cheaper to buy
To introduce contrasting line and detail on top of soft colour
To stop the paper drying out permanently
To remove the need for any composition
questions.explain: Ink over a watercolour wash combines soft tonal colour with crisp linear detail for contrast.

questions.q: Which term describes an artwork that combines flat and three-dimensional elements projecting from a surface?
questions.explain: Assemblage combines found objects and materials into a three-dimensional work projecting from a surface.

questions.q: A student layers wax crayon, then paints over it with a diluted colour wash. What effect is being used?
options: Wax resist, where the wax repels the water-based paint
Impasto, where paint is applied very thickly
questions.explain: Wax resist works because the oily wax repels the water-based wash, leaving the crayon marks showing through.

questions.q: A student wants a textured background with layered colour and torn imagery before adding fine pen detail. Which sequence works best?
options: Fine pen detail first, then glue paper, then paint
Collage torn paper, apply colour washes, then add pen detail on top
Paint, then wash it off completely, then draw
Add pen detail, then cover the whole piece in thick gesso
questions.explain: Building broad layers first and adding fine detail last keeps the delicate pen marks visible on top.

questions.q: What is the main benefit of experimenting with combined media before a final piece?
options: It guarantees a higher price for the artwork
It lets the artist test how materials interact and select effective combinations
It removes the need to consider composition
It means no preliminary studies are ever required
questions.explain: Experimentation reveals how materials behave together so the artist can choose the most effective combinations.

questions.q: Which craft process involves interlacing threads or yarns to create a textile?
questions.explain: Weaving interlaces warp and weft threads to produce a textile.

questions.q: What is the printmaking process of cutting a design into lino and printing from the raised surface called?
questions.explain: Lino printing is a relief process where ink is taken from the raised, uncut surface of the block.

questions.q: Which craft process shapes and hardens clay into ceramic objects?
options: Pottery, using techniques such as coiling and firing
questions.explain: Pottery shapes clay by methods such as coiling or throwing and hardens it through firing in a kiln.

questions.q: Why is clay usually fired in a kiln after it has been shaped and dried?
options: To make it soft and workable again
To harden it permanently into durable ceramic
To make it dissolve in water
To bleach the colour out of it
questions.explain: Firing chemically hardens the clay into a permanent, durable ceramic that will not return to a workable state.

questions.q: In textiles, what does 'batik' use to create pattern before dyeing?
options: Wax applied to resist the dye
questions.explain: Batik applies wax to areas of cloth to resist dye, producing patterned designs.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a stencil in screen printing?
options: To block ink from passing through selected areas of the mesh
To colour the paper before printing
questions.explain: A stencil blocks the screen mesh so ink only passes through the open areas, forming the printed image.

questions.q: A student wants to repeat the same bold two-colour image several times by hand. Which craft process is most suitable?
options: Lino printing, inking and pressing the block for each copy
questions.explain: A lino block can be re-inked and printed repeatedly, making it ideal for producing multiple bold copies.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the formal elements of art and design?
questions.explain: Tone, describing lightness and darkness, is one of the formal elements.

questions.q: The formal element 'tone' refers to which quality?
options: The lightness or darkness of an area
questions.explain: Tone describes how light or dark an area is, and is used to create form and depth.

questions.q: How can an artist create the illusion of texture on a flat drawn surface?
options: By using mark-making such as hatching, stippling or frottage
questions.explain: Marks such as hatching, stippling and rubbings (frottage) suggest surface texture on a flat drawing.

questions.q: Which formal element most directly describes the path made by a moving point, such as an outline or contour?
questions.explain: Line is the formal element describing marks that define outlines, edges and contours.

questions.q: A student wants to make a foreground object appear rounded and solid rather than flat. Which formal element should they focus on developing?
options: Tone, using shading to suggest three-dimensional form
Bright flat colour with no shadows
questions.explain: Graduated tone (shading) suggests light and shadow, making an object read as a rounded, solid form.

questions.q: Which pair are both recognised formal elements of art and design?
questions.explain: Colour and shape are both formal elements, alongside line, tone, form, texture and pattern.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Art & Design (1AD0) specification; Art, Craft and Design (Mixed Media)
